units.function: A 4,360-line customer-facing Agent control page combining identity and hierarchy, configuration and instructions, permissions, budgets, secrets, Runs and live logs, tool decisions, audit, revisions, built-in operations and responsive navigation.
units.dependencyDirection: The React page directly composes twelve API domains, global company/sidebar/experimental contexts, vendor adapter registries and capabilities, WebSocket transport, configuration and transcript parsers, instructions/assets/tools/Skills, budgets/trust, audit and built-in Agent controls. Presentation depends on application APIs, runtime-specific types and client-local policy in one monolith.
units.keyDataModels: Agent and reporting chain, membership and responsibleUserId, HeartbeatRun/events/logs/workspace operations/context snapshots, Work, budget policy, permissions/trust presets, config revisions, instruction bundles/files/assets, tool decisions, adapter configuration/capabilities, sessions and API keys.
units.lifecycle: Resolve company/Agent; fetch broad operational and governance projections; mutate Agent/config/permissions/budget/instructions/keys; approve or invoke/reset built-ins; monitor/cancel/resume/retry Runs; reconnect live event/log streams; render transcript/failure/event evidence; preserve selected dirty editors and route identity.
units.testAssessment: The three focused supporting suites passed 22/22 tests on 2026-08-19 and the complete UI no-emit TypeScript check passed. Tests give useful coverage for instruction editor selection/save, Run-to-Work navigation and progress/rename helpers, but do not cover most page mutations, tenant authorization, concurrency, approvals, secrets, API keys, WebSocket gap recovery, log integrity/redaction, bulk recovery, responsive accessibility or an end-to-end responsibility chain.
units.designRationale: Provide one operational surface where an administrator can configure an Agent and diagnose its latest and historical activity without navigating across many separate products. Rich client-side composition allows rapid feature addition and vendor-specific diagnostics.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an Agent Boss surface connecting organization, accountable humans, responsibility contracts, permissions/data grants, risk approval, vendor-neutral execution, evidence/results, costs and safe recovery while remaining independently deployable and responsive.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the page as Company OS-owned projections and bounded workflows. ADAPT only isolated patterns: invalid reporting-chain admission, explicit desired-versus-actual/runtime state, revision visibility, byte-paged logs with visible limits, live-follow behavior, Run-to-Work fallback and responsive list/detail layout. Put identity, Secrets, governance, Connector execution, evidence and presentation behind independent server-owned contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: The page mostly models Agent operational ownership: responsibleUserId is shown as 'On behalf of', entity approval is one click, and recovery/config/permission/key actions lack the full initiator-accountable human-executor-approver-permission/data-evidence-result chain. Vendor sessions, client redaction and adapter result/transcript parsing can become mistaken for authoritative responsibility evidence.

securityFindings: Secret/path redaction is client-side and inconsistent; raw login stdout/stderr, command/cwd, adapter result JSON and excerpts can expose credentials, host topology, private reasoning or external sessions.

Configuration, permissions, instruction files, budget, approval, retry/resume/session reset and key revocation lack a consistently visible expected revision, reason, accountable approver, action digest and durable receipt.
Instruction image upload uses global selectedCompanyId while the page also carries explicit Agent companyId, creating a concrete cross-company scope mismatch risk during route/context lag.
WebSocket reconnect has no resume cursor or visible gap recovery; polling and malformed-event failures are silently ignored, so the displayed tail cannot prove evidence completeness.
JSONL parsing silently discards malformed records, invents missing timestamps and coerces unknown streams; string-length fallback may not match byte offsets for Unicode logs.
API keys have no visible scope, audience, expiry, last-used metadata, rotation policy or responsible-human approval; plaintext remains in component state until dismissal/unmount.
Vendor authentication and private session manipulation occur inside the generic page, conflicting with a secret-free, vendor-neutral Connector boundary.

Several full-list fetches and client-side sorts have no visible pagination, and resolving one responsible user fetches the company directory, increasing unnecessary tenant-data exposure and scale risk.
